accuracy.evidence: Every sum in the lab and items was recomputed: 5+7+3 = 15 by both joining orders; ten pairs 4+6, 2+8, 7+3; REST totals 6+4+7 = 17, 3+7+8 = 18, 9+1+5 = 15; doubles 6+6+3 = 15, 4+4+5 = 13, 7+7+2 = 16; children's answers 6+4+5 = 15, 8+2+3 = 13, 9+1+6 = 16. Parameterised items were enumerated by validate_lessons (every corner and the explanation states the answer). Standards wording checked against CCSS 1.OA.B.3 (example 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12) and 1.OA.A.2, and NC England Y2 'add three one-digit numbers'.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets slips documented for early addition (NCETM Y1–Y2 addition and subtraction ready-to-progress notes; Thompson's work on counting-on errors): forgetting the third addend (step 5 Ali/Dev/Hana, p5, challenge tag forgot), thinking order changes the total (step 1 predict, p3, m8, tag order), only looking at adjacent numbers for a 10 or a double (step 2 predict 4 and 8, step 4 'There is no double', tag apart), counting the 10 itself when counting on (Cal, Eli, m6, tag countstart) and writing ten and six as 106 (step 3 decoy 107, Ivy, tag write).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 595 Addition and subtraction within 20 (flagw20), 590 Number bonds (flagnb20) and 506 Addition in any order (flagaddord) work with two addends; no other lab merges three number cards whose ten-frames keep each addend's colour, so the learner literally sees 7 and 3 fill one frame. The 'who is right' step and the split-double step are specific to three addends.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers commutativity/associativity by producing 15 from two different first pairs before the banner states it. Coloured ten-frames show a pair making exactly one full frame (the card turns green), so 'make 10' is seen, not told. Picking a total after the ten forces ten-and-some-more place value, the doubles step handles sums with no ten, and checking three children's answers turns the common slips into things the learner diagnoses.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the task disproves: 'Yes, it changes' for reordering, '4 and 8' (the first and last) for the ten pair, '107' for 10 + 7, 'There is no double' when the 4s are split, and 'Nothing, he is right' for Ali's 10. The done message reports the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and named slips: pair and pair2 (3 + 8 = 11, not 10), write (106 is one hundred and six), ten1 (10 is ten ones), forgot (added only two numbers), countstart (start counting on at 11), order (any order gives the same total), notdub and apart (a double can be split). Wrong joins in the lab also say exactly what was added, e.g. '4 + 8 = 12, not 10.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid sentences are short and use the precise terms total, pair, make 10, double and count on. Canvas text is one short instruction per step; buttons say exactly what they do (Join 6 and 4, Total: 17, Ali says 10).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to all lessons. The four kid paragraphs each carry one strategy (any order; make 10; ten and some more with the 108 warning; doubles and checking). The adult text gives standards, the task order and the five named slips.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for all six steps and mid-task states (/workspace/shots/a3L-all, a3D2-all, a3mid). After the first pass the ten-frames were turned upright (2 × 5) so three cards fill the height with dots about 22 px across; merged cards show 12 as a full and part frame without overflow; total tiles are about 54 px tall; feedback wraps inside the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Join 5 and 7, Total: 18, Ali says 10), the canvas aria-label lists the cards and progress after each action, and messages are spoken with c.say.
